ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT — TRACKED-CHANGES REDLINE
Prepared for Client Review
Matter: Review Account Control Agreement Counterparty Paper (Contracts)

Markings legend: [REJECTED DEVIATION] = deletion of counterparty's changed text; [INSERTED—MUST RETAIN] = firm-standard text restored per playbook; [ACCEPTED CONCESSION] = deviation accepted per deal team instructions.

---

ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT

This ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT (this "Agreement") is made and entered into as of [DATE], by and among [CUSTOMER], a [STATE] [entity type] ("Customer"), [BANK], a national banking association ("Bank"), and [CREDITOR], a [STATE] [entity type] ("Secured Party").

WHEREAS, Customer maintains one or more deposit accounts (each, an "Account") with Bank, as more particularly described on Schedule 1 hereto and in the Account Details Annex attached as Annex A;

WHEREAS, Customer has granted, or will grant, a security interest in the Accounts to Secured Party pursuant to that certain Credit Agreement dated as of [DATE] (the "Credit Agreement");

WHEREAS, the parties intend this Agreement to perfect and enforce such security interest in the Accounts pursuant to the Uniform Commercial Code as in effect in [STATE] (the "UCC");

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements contained herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the parties agree as follows:

ARTICLE I: DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATION

Section 1.1. Definitions. As used in this Agreement, the following terms have the meanings specified below:

"Account" means each deposit account identified on Schedule 1, including all balances, funds, and other property on deposit therein, together with all interest, dividends, and other earnings accruing thereon.

"Account Details" means the account information set forth on Annex A, including account numbers, title, bank routing information, and authorized signatories.

"Bank" has the meaning given in the preamble.

"Business Day" means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday, or other day on which Bank is closed for business.

"Credit Agreement" has the meaning given in the recitals.

"Customer" has the meaning given in the preamble.

"Depository Bank Standard Form" means the Bank's standard Account Control Agreement form attached as Exhibit A, which sets forth the baseline terms and conditions required by Bank.

"Entitlement Holder" means, with respect to any Account, the person that is the holder of the entitlement order with respect to such Account.

"Event of Default" means an "Event of Default" as defined in the Credit Agreement.

"Insolvency Proceeding" means any bankruptcy, insolvency, receivership, or other proceeding under any applicable federal or state bankruptcy, insolvency, or similar law.

"Material Adverse Effect" means a material adverse effect on [INSERT—MUST RETAIN: (a) the business, operations, properties, assets, or financial condition of Customer, taken as a whole; (b) the ability of Customer to perform its obligations under this Agreement; or (c) the validity or enforceability of this Agreement or the security interest granted thereunder. For the avoidance of doubt, "Material Adverse Effect" does NOT include any effect resulting from (i) changes in general economic, financial, or market conditions, (ii) changes in GAAP or applicable laws or regulations, or (iii) the announcement or pendency of this Agreement or the transactions contemplated hereby.] [REJECTED DEVIATION: "Material Adverse Effect" shall exclude any effect arising from or relating to any regulatory action, inquiry, investigation, order, or directive issued by any governmental or regulatory authority, including any pending regulatory inquiry or investigation disclosed on Schedule 3.7.]

"Notice of Exclusive Control" means a written notice delivered by Secured Party to Bank in accordance with Section 4.2.

"Secured Party" has the meaning given in the preamble.

"Security Interest" means the security interest in the Accounts granted by Customer to Secured Party under the Credit Agreement, as perfected through this Agreement.

"Survival Period" has the meaning specified in Section 7.3.

"UCC" has the meaning given in the recitals.

Section 1.2. Interpretation. Unless otherwise defined, capitalized terms used herein have the meanings assigned in the Credit Agreement and, if not therein defined, in the UCC. This Agreement may be executed in counterparts. Section headings are for convenience only and do not affect interpretation.

ARTICLE II: PERFECTION

Section 2.1. Grant of Control. Customer and Bank hereby acknowledge that Secured Party has, and shall have, control (within the meaning of Section 9-104 of the UCC) over each Account.

Section 2.2. Bank Agreement. Bank agrees to comply with all entitlement orders and instructions originated by Secured Party with respect to each Account without further consent by Customer.

Section 2.3. No Adverse Claims. Bank represents that it does not know of any lien, claim, encumbrance, or adverse claim against any Account other than (a) the security interests created pursuant to the Credit Agreement and this Agreement, and (b) those disclosed on Schedule 2.3.

ARTICLE III: COVENANTS

Section 3.1. Customer Covenants. Customer covenants and agrees that it shall: (a) not change the name, jurisdiction of organization, or organizational structure of Customer in any manner that would render any financing statement materially misleading; (b) not allow any third party (other than Bank) to have control over any Account; (c) provided that the information set forth in Annex A is and remains true, correct, and complete.

Section 3.2. Bank Covenants. Bank covenants and agrees that it shall: (a) keep accurate books and records with respect to each Account; (b) maintain each Account in accordance with its standard banking practices; and (c) comply with all instructions and entitlement orders from Secured Party as required by Section 2.2.

Section 3.3. [INSERTED—MUST RETAIN: Regulatory Inquiries. Customer shall promptly notify Secured Party of any regulatory inquiry, investigation, order, or directive issued or threatened by any governmental or regulatory authority with respect to any Account, Customer, or any property subject to this Agreement. For the avoidance of doubt, the existence of the two pending regulatory inquiries disclosed on Schedule 3.7 shall not be deemed to constitute a Material Adverse Effect, and the parties acknowledge that Schedule 3.7 is only a disclosure schedule and does not by itself diminish any representation, warranty, or covenant under this Agreement.] [REJECTED DEVIATION: No new Section 3.3 was proposed; the omission of regulatory notification obligations would leave Secured Party without notice of regulatory events that may affect any Account.]

ARTICLE IV: NOTICE OF EXCLUSIVE CONTROL

Section 4.1. Application of Funds. Pending the delivery of a Notice of Exclusive Control, Customer may continue to direct Bank with respect to the use and disposition of funds in the Accounts, and Bank may act on such directions.

Section 4.2. Notice of Exclusive Control. Secured Party may deliver a Notice of Exclusive Control to Bank upon the occurrence and during the continuance of an Event of Default. Such notice shall become effective upon receipt by Bank.

Section 4.3. Actions Following Notice. Within two (2) Business Days following receipt of a Notice of Exclusive Control, Bank shall: (a) cease complying with instructions originated by Customer with respect to the Accounts; and (b) comply with all instructions originated by Secured Party with respect to the Accounts.

Section 4.4. Entitlement Orders. Bank shall comply with all entitlement orders or other instructions originated by Secured Party with respect to the Accounts, whether or not a Notice of Exclusive Control has been delivered, so long as such instructions are consistent with Section 2.2.

ARTICLE V: REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES

Section 5.1. Customer Representations. Customer represents and warrants as of the date hereof and as of the date of each Transaction Date that: (a) Customer is duly organized, validly existing, and in good standing under the laws of its jurisdiction of organization; (b) Customer has full power and authority to enter into and perform this Agreement; (c) this Agreement constitutes Customer's legal, valid, and binding obligation; (d) no consent, approval, or notice to or filing with any governmental authority is required in connection with this Agreement; (e) Customer owns each Account free and clear of all liens and encumbrances except for the Security Interest and those disclosed on Schedule 5.1; and (f) the information set forth in Annex A is true, correct, and complete in all material respects.

Section 5.2. Retained Liabilities. [INSERTED—MUST RETAIN: Customer acknowledges that the liabilities identified on Schedule 5.2 (the "Retained Liabilities") are and shall remain exclusively Customer's obligations and shall not be assumed, discharged, or otherwise affected by this Agreement, and any indemnification obligations of Secured Party with respect to any Retained Liability are limited to the indemnification cap set forth in Section 7.1.] [REJECTED DEVIATION: The party markup proposed no corresponding provision to preserve the allocation of Retained Liabilities as identified on Schedule 5.2. The interplay between the markup's reduced indemnification cap and the Retained Liabilities would impermissibly shift economic risk to Secured Party.]

Section 5.3. Bank Representations. Bank represents and warrants to Secured Party that: (a) Bank has full power and authority to enter into and perform this Agreement; and (b) this Agreement constitutes Bank's legal, valid, and binding obligation.

ARTICLE VI: CONDITIONS PRECEDENT

Section 6.1. Conditions to Effectiveness. This Agreement shall become effective upon Bank's execution and delivery of this Agreement to Secured Party and Customer, and satisfaction of the conditions set forth in Section 6.2.

Section 6.2. Conditions. The effectiveness of this Agreement is subject to: (a) execution and delivery of this Agreement by each of the parties; (b) delivery of a certificate of the Secretary or Assistant Secretary of Customer attaching resolutions authorizing this Agreement; (c) delivery of a good standing certificate for Customer; and (d) payment of Bank's fees as set forth in the Depository Bank Standard Form.

ARTICLE VII: INDEMNIFICATION, LIMITATION, AND SURVIVAL

Section 7.1. Indemnification by Customer. Customer shall indemnify and hold harmless Secured Party and its affiliates, officers, directors, employees, agents, and advisors (each an "Indemnitee") from and against any and all losses, claims, damages, liabilities, and related expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees) incurred by any Indemnitee arising out of or relating to: (a) any breach by Customer of any representation, warranty, covenant, or obligation of Customer under this Agreement; or (b) any claim arising out of any Account or the use or disposition of funds therein. [REJECTED DEVIATION: The counterparty markup silently reduced the cap on Customer's indemnification obligations from 100% of the aggregate Amounts on Deposit in the Accounts to 50% thereof. The firm-standard cap of 100% of aggregate Amounts on Deposit is restored.] The aggregate liability of Customer under this Section 7.1 shall not exceed one hundred percent (100%) of the aggregate amounts on deposit in the Accounts [INSERTED—MUST RETAIN: as of the date the claim or liability first arose, before any applicable deductions, fees, or offsets].

Section 7.2. Indemnification by Bank. Bank shall indemnify and hold harmless Secured Party and Customer from and against any and all losses, claims, damages, liabilities, and related expenses incurred by any such person arising out of Bank's failure to comply with its obligations under this Agreement, including failure to comply with instructions from Secured Party as required herein.

Section 7.3. Limitation Period and Survival. [INSERTED—MUST RETAIN: The representations and warranties set forth in Article V shall survive the date of this Agreement and remain in full force and effect for a period of [thirty-six (36)] months following the termination of this Agreement.] [REJECTED DEVIATION: The counterparty markup shortened the survival period for the core representations from thirty-six (36) months to eighteen (18) months. This limitation-period reduction is contrary to Exhibit B (the survival matrix) and is rejected as a walk-away issue. The survival period for the core representations enumerated in Exhibit B shall remain thirty-six (36) months.] The survival provisions set forth in Exhibit B shall govern the survival of each representation and covenant.

Section 7.4. Basket. [ACCEPTED CONCESSION: Pursuant to the deal team's controlling instruction, the parties agree that any claims for indemnification under Section 7.1 shall not be asserted until the aggregate amount of such claims exceeds [AMOUNT] (the "Basket"). Once the Basket is exceeded, the full amount of all claims (including amounts under the Basket) may be recoverable. Customer and the deal team have agreed to accept the conversion of the basket from a deductible (i.e., only claims in excess of the Basket amount are recoverable) to a tipping basket (i.e., once the Basket threshold is crossed, claims are recoverable from the first dollar).]

Section 7.5. Material Adverse Effect. [REJECTED DEVIATION: The counterparty markup added carve-outs to the definition of "Material Adverse Effect" that would exclude regulatory actions, inquiries, investigations, orders, or directives issued by any governmental or regulatory authority. Given that Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries, and given the regulatory environment in which Customer operates, the proposed carve-outs would make the "Material Adverse Effect" standard unenforceable in circumstances precisely like those at issue in this matter. The firm-standard definition of "Material Adverse Effect" (which contains no such regulatory carve-outs) is restored as set forth in Section 1.1.]

ARTICLE VIII: MISCELLANEOUS

Section 8.1. Notices. All notices, consents, requests, and other communications under this Agreement shall be in writing and delivered to the respective addresses set forth on Schedule 1.

Section 8.2. Amendments and Waivers. No amendment, modification, or waiver of any provision of this Agreement shall be effective unless in writing and signed by each of the parties.

Section 8.3. Successors and Assigns. This Agreement shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of the parties and their respective successors and permitted assigns.

Section 8.4. Governing Law. This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of [STATE], without regard to conflicts-of-law principles.

Section 8.5. Severability. If any provision of this Agreement is held invalid or unenforceable, the remaining provisions shall continue in full force and effect.

Section 8.6. Entire Agreement. This Agreement, together with the Credit Agreement, the Schedules, and the Exhibits, constitutes the entire agreement among the parties with respect to the subject matter hereof.

Section 8.7. Counterparts. This Agreement may be executed in any number of counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original, and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument.

Section 8.8. Counterparty Markup Conformity. [INSERTED—MUST RETAIN: This Agreement, as finalized herein, reflects the firm-standard provisions required by the internal Account Control Agreement playbook, as reconciled against the executed Credit Agreement, the Depository Bank Standard Form, the account details set forth in Annex A, and the terms set forth in the Schedules and Exhibits. Any term in the counterparty's markup that is inconsistent with, or omitted from, the playbook, the Credit Agreement, the Depository Bank Standard Form, or the account details is hereby superseded by this Agreement.]

[Signature pages omitted.]

---

SCHEDULES AND EXHIBITS

Schedule 1: Account Information
[Insert account numbers, titles, and related information as set forth in Annex A]

Schedule 2.3: Known Liens and Claims
[As disclosed; no undisclosed claims.]

Schedule 3.7: Pending Regulatory Inquiries
[As disclosed in the base materials; two pending regulatory inquiries exist at the date of this Agreement. These are disclosed by way of qualification only and do not by themselves establish a Material Adverse Effect, and the counterparty's proposed MAE carve-outs materially change the standard of disclosure and are rejected.]

Schedule 5.1: Permitted Liens
[As disclosed.]

Schedule 5.2: Retained Liabilities
[As disclosed in the base materials; these liabilities remain with Customer and are not assumed by Secured Party.]

Exhibit A: Depository Bank Standard Form (incorporated by reference)
Exhibit B: Survival Matrix
[As set forth in the base materials; survival periods for core representations fixed at thirty-six (36) months, with other survival periods as described in the matrix. Any modification to the survival periods in the counterparty markup is rejected.]

Annex A: Account Details
[Account numbers, titles, authorized signatories, and related information as set forth in the account details referenced in the engagement materials.]

---

END OF REDLINE

PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT

MEMORANDUM

TO: Deal Team
FROM: [Counsel]
DATE: [Date]
RE: Account Control Agreement — Counterparty Markup Deviation Analysis, Issues, Risk Assessment, and Recommended Positions

---

This memorandum identifies every deviation, missing protection, and off-market term in the counterparty's markup of the Account Control Agreement (the "ACA"), assessed against the governing internal playbook, the executed Credit Agreement, the Depository Bank Standard Form, the account details, and related correspondence and checklists. All section references are to the draft ACA as redlined.

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

The counterparty's markup accepts most firm-standard provisions but introduces four material deviations that are analyzed below. Of these, the deal team's controlling instruction concedes the basket conversion but treats any survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue. The remaining deviations — the reduced indemnification cap, the Material Adverse Effect ("MAE") carve-outs for regulatory actions, and the shortened survival period — each require rejection and restoration of firm-standard terms.

---

ISSUE 1: INDEMNIFICATION CAP — SILENTLY REDUCED

Section References: Section 7.1 (Indemnification by Customer); Schedule 5.2 (Retained Liabilities)

Playbook Requirement: The internal playbook establishes a firm-standard cap on Customer's indemnification obligations of 100% of aggregate amounts on deposit in the Accounts. The counterparty's markup silently reduces this cap to 50%.

Risk Rating: HIGH

Description of Deviation: The counterparty's revision reduces the indemnification cap from 100% of aggregate amounts on deposit to 50% of such amounts, without any corresponding concession or explanatory note in the markup.

Exposure Analysis: This reduction would cap Secured Party's recovery for losses arising from Customer's breach of representations, warranties, covenants, or obligations at 50% of the amounts on deposit. Where the aggregate amounts on deposit are significant, this could result in a multi-million dollar shortfall in recovery for losses that are squarely within Customer's indemnifiable obligations. Critically, Schedule 5.2 identifies Retained Liabilities that must remain exclusively Customer's obligations. The reduced cap would combine with the Retained Liabilities to shift a material portion of the economic risk to Secured Party, precisely the sort of silent risk shifting that the playbook prohibits.

Interplay with Schedules: Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities that the markup's indemnification changes would silently shift. Under the firm-standard position, the cap remains at 100%, ensuring that any losses from retained liabilities are fully indemnified to the extent they fall within the scope of Section 7.1.

Recommended Position: REJECT. Restore the firm-standard indemnification cap of 100% of aggregate amounts on deposit in the Accounts, as set forth in the redline. No reasonable concession on the indemnification cap is warranted, particularly given the pending regulatory inquiries disclosed on Schedule 3.7 and the potential for losses arising from Customer's operations.

---

ISSUE 2: INDEMNIFICATION BASKET — CONVERTED FROM DEDUCTIBLE TO TIPPING

Section References: Section 7.4 (Basket)

Playbook Requirement: The internal playbook requires a deductible basket arrangement, under which claims for indemnification are recoverable only to the extent they exceed the Basket threshold.

Description of Deviation: The counterparty's markup converts the basket from a deductible to a tipping basket, under which once the Basket threshold is exceeded, claims are recoverable from the first dollar (i.e., the full amount, including amounts below the Basket threshold, becomes recoverable).

Risk Rating: MODERATE

Deal Team Instruction: The deal team correspondence (id. 110) states in the latest controlling message that the client will CONCEDE the basket conversion from a deductible to a tipping basket. Earlier messages expressing the opposite priority ordering are superseded and do not control.

Exposure Analysis: While this conversion increases Secured Party's potential recovery, the deal team has expressly instructed that this is an acceptable concession. The practical exposure from the tipping basket is the incremental recovery between the first dollar and the Basket threshold, which is not a walk-away matter for the deal team.

Recommended Position: ACCEPT, per deal team instruction. The basket conversion is acceptable and should be incorporated into the final agreement as reflected in the redline (Section 7.4).

---

ISSUE 3: MATERIAL ADVERSE EFFECT — ADDED CARVE-OUTS FOR REGULATORY ACTION

Section References: Section 1.1 (Definition of Material Adverse Effect); Section 3.3 (Regulatory Inquiries); Schedule 3.7 (Pending Regulatory Inquiries)

Playbook Requirement: The internal playbook requires a firm-standard MAE definition that does NOT include carve-outs for regulatory action. The Standard Definition of MAE includes the three-part standard: (a) business/operations, (b) ability to perform, and (c) validity of transaction/security interest.

Description of Deviation: The counterparty's markup adds carve-outs to the MAE definition that would exclude any effect arising from or relating to any regulatory action, inquiry, investigation, order, or directive issued by any governmental or regulatory authority, including any pending regulatory inquiry or investigation disclosed on Schedule 3.7.

Risk Rating: HIGH

Exposure Analysis: This carve-out is especially concerning because Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries of exactly the kind that the markup carves out. In substance, the counterparty seeks to define away MAE events arising from precisely the type of regulatory exposure currently facing Customer. If the MAE carve-out were accepted, Secured Party would be prevented from invoking an MAE-based remedy even where a regulatory action causes a material adverse effect on Customer's business or on the value of the Accounts. This renders the MAE standard hollow in the exact scenario for which it was designed to protect Secured Party.

Interplay with Schedule 3.7: The counterparty's carve-out is not merely an abstract risk; it is directly aligned with the pending regulatory inquiries disclosed on Schedule 3.7. The proposed carve-out would preclude MAE-based remedies for these regulatory actions. The schedules notably confirm that the pending regulatory inquiries exist at the date of the agreement and that their existence is disclosed by way of qualification only, without diminishing any representations or covenants.

Recommended Position: REJECT. Restore the firm-standard MAE definition as set forth in Section 1.1 in the redline. Additionally, restore the proposed Section 3.3 requiring Customer to promptly notify Secured Party of any regulatory inquiry, investigation, order, or directive, so that Secured Party has full visibility into regulatory developments affecting the Accounts.

---

ISSUE 4: SURVIVAL PERIOD — SHORTENED FOR CORE REPRESENTATIONS

Section References: Section 7.3 (Limitation Period and Survival); Exhibit B (Survival Matrix)

Playbook Requirement: The internal playbook, as incorporated in Exhibit B (survival matrix), fixes the survival period for core representations at thirty-six (36) months following termination. This is the firm-standard survival period for the core representations enumerated in Exhibit B.

Description of Deviation: The counterparty's markup shortens the survival period for the core representations from thirty-six (36) months to eighteen (18) months.

Risk Rating: CRITICAL

Deal Team Instruction: The deal team correspondence (id. 110) states in the latest controlling message that the client treats any survival-period reduction as a WALK-AWAY ISSUE. This is the most severe risk rating in this analysis and reflects the immediate and non-negotiable rejection of this deviation.

Exposure Analysis: Shortening the survival period from thirty-six (36) months to eighteen (18) months would cut in half the duration of Secured Party's ability to bring claims for breaches of core representations and warranties. Given the pending regulatory inquiries on Schedule 3.7, which may only become fully manifest well after the shortened eighteen-month window, this reduction could extinguish Secured Party's remedies before the full extent of potential losses from regulatory action is known. The reduction directly contradicts Exhibit B's survival matrix and constitutes a material reallocation of risk that the deal team has designated as a walk-away threshold.

Interplay with Exhibit B: Exhibit B (the survival matrix) controls the survival schedule for each representation and covenant. The markup's limitation-period change directly contradicts the survival matrix, and Exhibit B expressly controls over general statements in the base contract materials.

Recommended Position: REJECT — WALK-AWAY ISSUE. Under no circumstances should the survival-period reduction be accepted. Restore the thirty-six (36) month survival period for all core representations as set forth in Exhibit B and reflected in the redline (Section 7.3). If the counterparty insists on this reduction, the matter should be escalated for deal termination consideration.

---

SUMMARY DEVIATION MATRIX

| # | Section | Deviation | Playbook Requirement | Risk Rating | Recommended Position |
|---|---------|-----------|----------------------|-------------|---------------------|
| 1 | §7.1 | Indemnification cap reduced from 100% to 50% of aggregate amounts on deposit | Cap at 100% of aggregate amounts on deposit | HIGH | REJECT — restore 100% cap |
| 2 | §7.4 | Basket converted from deductible to tipping | Deductible basket | MODERATE | ACCEPT — per deal team concession |
| 3 | §1.1, §3.3 | MAE definition adds carve-outs for regulatory action | Standard MAE definition; no regulatory carve-outs | HIGH | REJECT — restore standard MAE definition and add regulatory notification covenant |
| 4 | §7.3 | Survival period for core representations shortened from 36 to 18 months | Survival per Exhibit B (36 months for core reps) | CRITICAL | REJECT — WALK-AWAY ISSUE; restore 36-month survival per Exhibit B |

---

ADDITIONAL OBSERVATIONS

1. Distractor Material: Document 58, functionally a misfiled administrative correspondence relating to an unrelated engagement, was not relied upon in this analysis and should be disregarded.

2. Schedule 3.7: The two pending regulatory inquiries disclosed on Schedule 3.7 confirm the real-world significance of the markup's MAE carve-outs. Counsel should verify that no additional regulatory inquiries have arisen since the schedule date before execution.

3. Schedule 5.2: The Retained Liabilities listed on Schedule 5.2 remain Customer's exclusive obligations under Section 5.2 as restored in the redline. The redline preserves the economic allocation explicit in the base materials.

4. Exhibit B: The survival matrix controls over any general statement in the base contract materials, per the directive in the engagement materials. The redline accordingly restores Exhibit B's survival schedule.

5. Template Conformity: Section 8.8 (Counterparty Markup Conformity) is inserted to confirm that the final Agreement conforms to the internal playbook, the executed Credit Agreement, the Depository Bank Standard Form, the account details in Annex A, and the terms of the Schedules and Exhibits. This provision protects against any future argument that the counterparty markup's changes should be effective where they were not expressly tracked or reconciled.

---

RECOMMENDED NEGOTIATION STRATEGY

1. Lead with the survival-period reduction as the walk-away threshold. Communicate in no uncertain terms that the eighteen-month survival period is unacceptable and that the thirty-six month period per Exhibit B is non-negotiable.

2. On the MAE carve-outs and indemnification cap, reject firmly but acknowledge the possibility of commercial compromise on the indemnification cap (e.g., negotiate a middle ground such as 75% of aggregate amounts on deposit) only if the MAE carve-outs are dropped entirely and the survival period is retained at thirty-six months.

3. On the basket conversion, accept per deal team instruction without conceding anything further.

4. On Schedule 3.7 regulatory inquiries, direct the deal team to work with Customer to obtain updated disclosure confirming whether any new regulatory actions have been initiated since the date of the schedule.

---

This memorandum is privileged and confidential, prepared in anticipation of litigation and for the provision of legal advice. Please contact counsel with any questions.
